Alice Chen: quick heads-up — parity check failing for replay harness after kernel v2.3 rollout. synthetic microbenchmarks look fine, but replay (prod traces) shows ~8-12% higher P95 token latency and ~4% token-cost increase for cohort C3. no obvious correctness diffs, just perf. anyone seen this pattern?
Ravi Patel: hmm. are we sure the replay run used the exact same batching mode and kv-warmup as prod? sometimes kernel swaps change batching heuristics mapping. :thinking_face:
Samir Gupta: top suspects: 1) kv cache warmup differences (replay may not populate prefixes the same way), 2) non-deterministic kernel scheduling causing different batching combos, 3) anonymization/sampling biasing trace tail.
Alice Chen: good call. we switched anonymization -> stratified sampling last quarter to reduce PII risk; sample rate also dropped from 1% -> 0.1% for C3. that could change seq_len dist.
replay-bot: run results: https://ci.internal/runs/98523 — replay vs prod payloads + diffs. (run id: 98523)
Katie Lopez: grabbed the diff for the hot path. small excerpt: ```bash
# replay run command we used
replay-run --trace cohort-C3 --anon=stratified --sample-rate=0.001 --seed=1234 --batcher=dynamic --kernel=v2.3 --kv-warmup=0
# summary
p50 34ms -> 36ms
p95 120ms -> 137ms
tokens/sec ~ -4%
```
Ravi Patel: two quick experiments to do (apples-to-apples):
- run replay with batcher=legacy and kernel=v2.3 (to see batching heuristic impact)
- run replay with kv-warmup=prefix (replay populate prefixes to mimic prod)
Also ensure seed fixed and the replay worker affinity matches prod (same CPU/GPU pairing).
Samir Gupta: I inspected profiler flame graphs from the run (linked in the CI artifacts). looks like more frequent short-lived kernel launches and lower batch sizes hitting the GPU. could be kernel selector choosing a narrower kernel because seq_len distribution shifted. if batch size drops, latency P95 jumps.
Alice Chen: ok let's try those two runs. Ravi, can you own the replays? if we still see delta, next step is instrumenting the runtime to log per-request chosen kernel id + batch size and attach to replay traces.
Ravi Patel: I'll queue them now. also adding a control: replay with anonymization=none + sample-rate=0.01 to match old distribution. will compare synthetic-run (deterministic synthetic traffic) -> replay-with-prod-seq-dist -> prod. should give us synthetic vs prod vs replay triage.
Katie Lopez: note: when we flip kv-warmup=prefix, make sure to include the same prefix-cache TTL and disable cache-eviction emulation in the harness. small differences there can hide the real effect.
Samir Gupta: if we still see kernel mis-selection, we might need to pin kernel selection to baseline (KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy) and re-run. that will tell us if the heuristics change is the culprit. also capture nvprof + timings per kernel.
replay-bot: queued replay-run #98601 (owner: Ravi Patel) — link: https://ci.internal/runs/98601
Alice Chen: thanks all — Ravi please paste logs when done. assigning follow-ups: Ravi = run + logs, Samir = profiler diffs, Katie = sample-dist comparison notes. :thumbsup:
Ravi Patel: on it. ETA ~ 45m.
replay-bot: run #98601 completed. artifacts: https://ci.internal/runs/98601/artifacts (includes kernel_id logs and batch_size histogram)
Ravi Patel: preliminary quick look: batch_size histogram for replay (v2.3) shows 20% more single-request batches vs prod. kernel_id trace shows fallback to narrow-kernel in those cases. attaching short excerpt in thread.
Samir Gupta: that points squarely to batching heuristics interacting with kernel selector. next step: try legacy batcher + v2.3, and also run v2.2 w/ dynamic batcher as a control.
Alice Chen: excellent. keep updates here. once we isolate, we'll plan a mitigation: either revert heuristic or force kernel mapping for the affected seq_len range.
Ravi Patel: noted. I'll run the two control replays and post results.
Katie Lopez: thanks — also logging this as a perf-regression ticket and linking the replay artifacts.
